evidence.claim: Rolling hills, farmland and waterfalls along two Pennsylvania state routes
evidence.quote: With rolling hillsides, picturesque farmlands, quaint B&amp;Bs, rushing waterfalls, beautiful woodlands, historical treasures, and the architectural gems of Frank Lloyd Wright, the 68-mile Laurel Highlands Scenic Byway offers a delight-filled journey along Routes 711 and 381.

evidence.claim: The Laurel Highlands Scenic Byway follows 68 miles of Routes 711 and 381 through rolling hills, farmland and woodland.
evidence.quote: With rolling hillsides, picturesque farmlands, quaint B&amp;Bs, rushing waterfalls, beautiful woodlands, historical treasures, and the architectural gems of Frank Lloyd Wright, the 68-mile Laurel Highlands Scenic Byway offers a delight-filled journey along Routes 711 and 381.

evidence.claim: VisitPA highlights waterfalls and Frank Lloyd Wright buildings along the drive.
evidence.quote: rushing waterfalls, beautiful woodlands, historical treasures, and the architectural gems of Frank Lloyd Wright

evidence.claim: On its southern section, Route 381 curves through forests and fields, crosses the Youghiogheny River at Ohiopyle and passes through tracts of Forbes State Forest near the West Virginia line.
evidence.quote: From the state line, the route heads north on two-lane undivided Wharton Furnace Road, passing through woodland with some farms and homes as it runs through tracts of the Forbes State Forest.

evidence.claim: On its southern section, Route 381 curves through forests and fields, crosses the Youghiogheny River at Ohiopyle and passes through tracts of Forbes State Forest near the West Virginia line.
evidence.quote: The road curves to the east and heads through more forests before turning northeast into a mix of farmland and woodland with a few residences.

evidence.claim: On its southern section, Route 381 curves through forests and fields, crosses the Youghiogheny River at Ohiopyle and passes through tracts of Forbes State Forest near the West Virginia line.
evidence.quote: PA 381 passes a few homes prior to crossing the Youghiogheny River on the Ohiopyle Highway Bridge

evidence.claim: The Laurel Highlands byway designation took effect on September 11, 1996, joining portions of PA 711 and PA 381 into a corridor from the Conemaugh River to West Virginia.
evidence.quote: LAUREL HIGHLANDS Effective: September 11, 1996 District: 12-0 Counties: Westmoreland and Fayette State Routes: 0711 and 0381, Laurel Highlands State Route 711 from the Conemaugh River to the Jones Mills, continuing along Routes 711/381 South to Normalville and along Route 381 to the State Line of West Virginia.

evidence.claim: The numbered highway came before the scenic designation: PA 711 was first signed in 1928, with construction continuing into the early 1930s.
evidence.quote: The route was first signed in 1928, but construction along the route did not get completed until the early 1930s.

evidence.claim: In the 1950s, its southern endpoint moved from Pleasant Grove to Belle Vernon; another move in the 1960s established the current endpoint at Connellsville.
evidence.quote: In the 1950s, the route's southern terminus was moved from Pleasant Grove to PA 71 at the intersection at I-70 in the borough of Belle Vernon.  In the 1960s, the southern terminus was moved yet again to its current location.

evidence.claim: In the 1950s, its southern endpoint moved from Pleasant Grove to Belle Vernon; another move in the 1960s established the current endpoint at Connellsville.
evidence.quote: The route begins at an intersection of US 119 and PA 201 in the western part of the city of Connellsville.

evidence.claim: The Ohiopyle crossing is a two-lane highway bridge opened in 1975, the third bridge in that vicinity, following a nineteenth-century covered bridge and a later Pratt truss.
evidence.quote: The Ohiopyle Highway Bridge is a structure that carries two lanes of Pennsylvania Route 381 over the Youghiogheny River in Ohiopyle, Pennsylvania, United States. The span, which opened in 1975, is the third to be located in the vicinity. An original 19th-century covered bridge was replaced by a Pratt truss bridge around 1900.

evidence.claim: Driving south from Seward, follow PA 711 through Ligonier and Stahlstown to Donegal.
evidence.quote: After PA 711 itself passes over the Pennsylvania Turnpike, the route passes through Donegal, and heads northeast to the village of Stahlstown

evidence.claim: Driving south from Seward, follow PA 711 through Ligonier and Stahlstown to Donegal.
evidence.quote: The route continues northeast to the borough of Ligonier

evidence.claim: Driving south from Seward, follow PA 711 through Ligonier and Stahlstown to Donegal.
evidence.quote: passes through the boroughs of New Florence and Seward.

evidence.claim: The byway continues through Jones Mills to Normalville, where PA 381 carries it south.
evidence.quote: State Route 711 from the Conemaugh River to the Jones Mills, continuing along Routes 711/381 South to Normalville and along Route 381 to the State Line of West Virginia.

evidence.claim: Beyond Mill Run, Fallingwater lies west of the road; then come Ohiopyle, Farmington and the final wooded stretch to the state line.
evidence.quote: The road continues through forests with some farm fields and homes, heading into Springfield Township at the point it crosses Laurel Run. The route heads north into open agricultural areas with some woods and residences, passing through Mill Run.

evidence.claim: Beyond Mill Run, Fallingwater lies west of the road; then come Ohiopyle, Farmington and the final wooded stretch to the state line.
evidence.quote: passes through Kauffman, at which point it heads to the east of Fallingwater

evidence.claim: Beyond Mill Run, Fallingwater lies west of the road; then come Ohiopyle, Farmington and the final wooded stretch to the state line.
evidence.quote: The route continues north and north-northeast and reaches an intersection with US 40 in Farmington.

evidence.claim: Beyond Mill Run, Fallingwater lies west of the road; then come Ohiopyle, Farmington and the final wooded stretch to the state line.
evidence.quote: crossing into forested Ohiopyle State Park. The route continues through the park and becomes Main Street as it heads into the borough of Ohiopyle

evidence.claim: Fort Ligonier began as the last fortified link on General John Forbes’s new road across Pennsylvania toward French-held Fort Duquesne.
evidence.quote: He ordered construction of a new road across Pennsylvania, guarded by a chain of fortifications, the final link being the "Post at Loyalhanna", fifty miles from his objective.

evidence.claim: Built in 1758, it served as a staging area for that campaign and later as a passage post to Fort Pitt.
evidence.quote: The fort served as a staging area for the Forbes Expedition of 1758.

evidence.claim: Built in 1758, it served as a staging area for that campaign and later as a passage post to Fort Pitt.
evidence.quote: The fort was constructed in September 1758.

evidence.claim: Built in 1758, it served as a staging area for that campaign and later as a passage post to Fort Pitt.
evidence.quote: It served as a post of passage to the new Fort Pitt

evidence.claim: The garrison was decommissioned in 1766.
evidence.quote: The fort was decommissioned from active service in 1766.

evidence.claim: What occupies the original site now is a reconstruction, opened in 1953 after archaeological work began in 1947.
evidence.quote: The first archaeological excavations of Fort Ligonier began in 1947.

evidence.claim: What occupies the original site now is a reconstruction, opened in 1953 after archaeological work began in 1947.
evidence.quote: In 1953, the fort was reconstructed on its original location and opened to the public.

evidence.claim: Wooden defenses, a moat and a storehouse give physical form to the post; the adjacent museum includes exhibits on the excavations that helped recover its layout.
evidence.quote: The reconstructed fort features wood fortifications, a moat, artillery, and several buildings including an officer’s headquarters, soldiers’ bunks, and a storehouse.

evidence.claim: Wooden defenses, a moat and a storehouse give physical form to the post; the adjacent museum includes exhibits on the excavations that helped recover its layout.
evidence.quote: Architect and historian Charles Morse Stotz oversaw the project and was tasked with identifying the fort's original location and layout.

evidence.claim: Wooden defenses, a moat and a storehouse give physical form to the post; the adjacent museum includes exhibits on the excavations that helped recover its layout.
evidence.quote: The museum houses exhibitions about the French and Indian War, the archaeological excavations of Fort Ligonier

evidence.claim: Fallingwater places part of a three-story country house directly over Bear Run’s waterfall.
evidence.quote: it is built partly over a waterfall on the Bear Run stream.

evidence.claim: Fallingwater places part of a three-story country house directly over Bear Run’s waterfall.
evidence.quote: The three-story residence was developed as a weekend retreat

evidence.claim: Frank Lloyd Wright designed it as a weekend retreat for Pittsburgh department-store owner Edgar J. Kaufmann Sr. and his wife Liliane.
evidence.quote: Designed by the architect Frank Lloyd Wright, it is built partly over a waterfall on the Bear Run stream. The three-story residence was developed as a weekend retreat for Edgar J. Kaufmann Sr., the owner of Kaufmann's Department Store in Pittsburgh, and his wife Liliane.

evidence.claim: The family began using the house in 1937; the guest wing followed in 1939.
evidence.quote: The Kaufmanns began using the house in 1937 and hired Wright to design a guest wing, which was finished in 1939.

evidence.claim: Its terraces extend from the chimney without supports at their outer ends.
evidence.quote: The house includes multiple outdoor terraces,  which are cantilevered, extending outward from a chimney without support at the opposite end.

evidence.claim: The terraces sagged, and major repairs in the late 1990s and early 2000s addressed structural defects and poor drainage.
evidence.quote: The house was renovated in the late 1990s and early 2000s to remedy severe structural defects, including sagging terraces and poor drainage.

evidence.claim: Local stone, reinforced concrete, steel and glass make up the house.
evidence.quote: Fallingwater is made of locally–quarried stone, reinforced concrete, steel, and plate glass.

evidence.claim: Notice the terraces extending outward from the chimney, unsupported at their outer ends.
evidence.quote: The house includes multiple outdoor terraces,  which are cantilevered, extending outward from a chimney without support at the opposite end.

evidence.claim: At Ohiopyle, a 20-foot waterfall spans the Youghiogheny River.
evidence.quote: Ohiopyle Falls is a 20-foot (6.1 m) waterfall that spans the Youghiogheny River

evidence.claim: Railroads once brought visitors from Pittsburgh to see the falls and stay in riverside resorts, where the attractions included dancing pavilions and bowling alleys.
evidence.quote: The railroads also brought tourists to Ohiopyle. The round trip ride from Pittsburgh to Ohiopyle was one dollar. Tourists flocked to the area to see the waterfalls and stay at the resorts that quickly sprouted up along the Youghiogheny River. The resorts had boardwalks, dancing pavilions, bowling alleys

evidence.claim: As automobile travel displaced that resort trade, the buildings were demolished and forest regrew.
evidence.quote: The rise of the automobile caused the end of the resorts at Ohiopyle. The buildings were torn down, and the forests were allowed to regrow.

evidence.claim: The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy bought the land and sold it to the Commonwealth.
evidence.quote: The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy purchased the land and then sold it to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

evidence.claim: Ohiopyle State Park opened in 1965, with formal dedication following in 1971.
evidence.quote: Ohiopyle State Park was opened to the public in 1965 and was formally dedicated on May 28, 1971.

evidence.claim: The falls now occupy the center of the park’s Falls Day Use Area.
evidence.quote: Ohiopyle Falls is a 20-foot (6.1 m) waterfall that spans the Youghiogheny River and is surrounded by the Falls Day Use Area located at the center of the park.

evidence.claim: The borough itself is surrounded by the state park.
evidence.quote: The borough is surrounded by Ohiopyle State Park.
